model.costScope: Full annual recipient expense including regrants, support costs and non-LA work, normalized to a prospective service cohort. This is not verified marginal cost. External partner costs unmeasured; explicit resource sensitivity only.
model.geographicAttribution: g=1 for the modeled LA Peacemakers participant branch within LA County. This is not a claim that all UPI activity or benefit is local; Orange residents qualify but no separate Orange benefit is invented. National training and statewide justice work remain unquantified.
model.formula: A(T,m,d)=sum(t=1..T)[((1-m)/(1+d))^t]; qd=u*A(T,m,d); qn=qa+du*A(Tn,m,d). E=sum(t=0..ceil(D)-1)[min(1,D-t)*((1-m)*rho/(1+d))^t]. V=N*r*e*a*b*E. Qall=V*(f*qd+(1-f)*qn)-H; QLA=V*(f*qd+(1-f)*qn)*g-H. price=10*C/QLA only if positive. Central D=1; downstream health starts at the avoided-event time, modeled as time zero of its exposure period.
model.counterfactual: Existing public GRYD/Safe Passage, separate BSCC training, committed philanthropy and spendable reserves continue. a discounts service benefit that persists without UPI; b discounts capacity not changed by a new ordinary gift. Central preserves one service year, not permanent program operation. The bridge scenario models a temporary service gap, not an extra annual cohort or permanent funding loss.
model.attribution: Only serious shooting/homicide participant victimization is modeled. UPI monitoring injury counts have broader/unclear definitions and do not supply the causal rate. Benefits to other victims, policy and training recipients are omitted. V already includes partner and donor additionality; no regrant, staff, retaliation or citywide-decline credit is added again.
model.uncertainty: Partial-health judgment central retained despite unobserved marginal parameters. Finite competing mortality and health loss are explicit judgments. Scenarios vary scale, risk, effect, funding, attribution, exposure, survival, local share and resource scope; no probabilistic quantiles or recipient-wide effectiveness claim. For multi-year stress cases, the expected-event calculation is a low-risk linear approximation, not a joint competing-risk simulation of repeated injury in the same person. It cannot support large extrapolations or infinite cohorts.
model.nativeOutcomes: Central expected net additional avoided victimizations 1.5404999999999998, including 0.3081 fatal events. These are fractional model expectations, not observed people saved.

inputs.name: C
inputs.unit: USD per annual full recipient budget
inputs.rationale: Original FY2025 expense, audited-total reconciliation and grants retained once.

inputs.name: N
inputs.unit: prospective engaged participant-equivalents for one full service year
inputs.rationale: 1,027 first-year enrollments anchors scale only; engagement and person-time not observed.

inputs.name: r
inputs.unit: serious shooting/homicide victimizations per participant-year without the modeled increment
inputs.rationale: Below annualized READI control benchmark; local mix and background declines uncertain.

inputs.name: e
inputs.rationale: 10% working transport judgment, not the READI TOT or GRYD retaliation coefficient.

inputs.name: f
inputs.unit: fatal share of avoided modeled victimizations
inputs.rationale: 20%; not estimated from the broadly defined UPI injury graph.

inputs.name: u
inputs.unit: health utility while alive after initially avoided death
inputs.rationale: .8 constant simplified utility, not measured recipient health.

inputs.name: T
inputs.unit: maximum downstream years after initially avoided death
inputs.rationale: 47-year finite cap, not a verified life expectancy.

inputs.name: m
inputs.unit: annual all-cause death probability conditional on being alive
inputs.rationale: 1% annual death probability in discrete survival (1-m)^t; includes continuing violence and other mortality. This is not a continuous hazard or an age-specific recipient life table.

inputs.name: qa
inputs.unit: acute QALYs lost per nonfatal injury
inputs.rationale: .1 immediate-area approximation; not derived from PTSD prevalence.

inputs.name: du
inputs.unit: annual chronic utility decrement per nonfatal injury
inputs.rationale: .05 across all survivors as an expected average, not everyone permanently disabled.

inputs.name: Tn
inputs.rationale: 10 years; beyond the observed follow-up and varied as a judgment.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: .75, separate from private gift response; no measured attributable fraction.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: .5 after secured funding, reserves, substitution and allocation; no verified gift-sized gap.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: LA share of modeled branch benefit
inputs.rationale: 1 for LA resident participant branch; local residence still to verify, no headquarters allocation.

inputs.name: H
inputs.unit: additional LA QALYs lost outside modeled victimizations
inputs.rationale: 0 central is not safety evidence; additive worker/privacy/displacement harm retained in stress.

inputs.name: D
inputs.unit: finite years of risk reduction for the same cohort
inputs.rationale: 1 central; fractional bridge and two-year cases cannot be read as repeated new cohorts.

inputs.name: rho
inputs.unit: annual persistence of relative effect after first year
inputs.rationale: 1 irrelevant for central D=1; .5 in durability-only second-year stress.

sensitivity: At $1 million per 10 QALYs, the branch requires 23.74 net additional avoided victimizations versus 1.5404999999999998; holding other central assumptions fixed would require e=1.541, greater than 1.
Each of N, r, e, a and b proportionally changes gross benefit; a better clinical conversion alone cannot resolve weak donor response. No threshold is a giving recommendation.
A two-year durability claim discounts second-year effect and survival. If a second funded service year is required, the second annual cost is included too; price does not simply halve.
Attribution/private response a=b=1 gives price/10=5778423.655214918; this is a diagnostic, not default.
Using comparable mean operating expense gives price/10=10030716.05711163; it is not a claim that current capacity can be bought at historical cost.
Zero/full replacement and net harm have no finite beneficial price. Joint favorable/low-positive cases carry no assigned probabilities.

The quarter-year bridge also raises b from 0.5 to 1: its benefit is one-half of central, not one-quarter. It represents a fully responsive three-month gap; retaining central b=0.5 would yield one-quarter of central benefit. No permanently unfunded year is inferred.
missingInputs: Correctly matched FY2025 audit and evidence recurring revenue-recognition controls were implemented; current cash restrictions, payables and board commitments.
Peacemakers post-2026 renewal and termination status by award, remaining cash obligation, marginal gift allocation, trained-worker recruitment/retention and funded versus unfunded person-time.
Coalition-to-Schedule-I reconciliation (18 initiative members versus 17 annual legal grant routes), fiscal sponsors and partner cofunding/overlap with approved Safe Passage contracts.
Unique annual engaged participants, intensity, incident definitions, untreated risk and residence; independently linked person-time outcomes with credible comparisons.
UPI-specific causal contribution rather than all GRYD/CVI effectiveness, displacement and other-victim effects, worker health/privacy burden and diminishing returns.
Age-specific survival and finite nonfatal utility loss; no empirical probability distribution or complete portfolio price.
model.nativeCosts: At central scale, full operating expense / 1,027 prospective engaged participant-equivalents is $8663.76; these are not verified engaged person-years. Full expense / 1.5405 modeled additional avoided victimizations is $5775841.61. Fatal events are 0.3081 of that total, not additional events. Finite survival and morbidity convert the mutually exclusive branches to QALYs.
